rationale: This is a cosmetic wrapper (IND_ZSCORE) placed on the archive's existing best performer with no change to the underlying economics, and while industry-tilt diagnostics have some value, a standardization-only respecification is exactly the kind of variant the objective warns against.

Replacing MUL with MIN is a genuine change in aggregation semantics (Leontief conjunction vs. multiplicative blend) that plausibly reconciles the archive's sign conflict, though the stated justification is partly wrong — a product of two IND_RANKs is monotone in each leg, not "non-monotone through the middle," so the real fix is distributional spread, not monotonicity.

The expression algebraically collapses to (capx − approximate operating cash flow)/assets, i.e. negative free cash flow / the financing deficit, which is a direct rediscovery of the well-documented free-cash-flow and net-external-financing anomalies rather than a new cross-theme interaction.

This opens a genuinely different accrual channel (purchase-accounting asset creation) benchmarked against physical capital formation, is internally consistent in sign, and is not a restatement of the working-capital legs already tested — though the reviewer should expect a large point mass at zero from firms with no intangibles and a volatile small-denominator tail.

Deleting the operating-liability term from the archive winner's numerator is a legitimate component decomposition but is incremental rather than substantively new, and the resulting quantity is close to a known operating-asset-growth measure with a different deflator.

The numerator TS_SUM of one-year DELTAs telescopes into a simple three-year level change, so the expression measures a longer-horizon change and cannot identify the "chronic/persistent reliance" the hypothesis claims (a firm with one large accrual year and two flat years scores identically to a steadily bloating one), making it a horizon rescaling of the winner rather than the stated persistence test.
